claims.text: Ab initio-based techniques with adaptive sampling can substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties for high-entropy systems.
The proposed method evaluates free energies for both solid and fluid high-entropy systems.
Adaptive sampling efficiently samples phase space.
Efficient adaptive sampling reduces the need for costly molecular dynamics.
The proposed approach retains or captures vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling.
The proposed approach will reduce computational cost by 50% relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The proposed approach will increase throughput by 20% relative to TOR-TILD for multicomponent high-entropy systems.
The proposed temperature boundary is 1000–3000 K.
The proposed composition boundary is systems containing 3–6 elements.
Differences greater than 10% in phase free energies relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics would falsify the hypothesis.
Differences greater than 5% in derived observables such as heat capacity or entropy relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics would falsify the hypothesis.
